about: Why a test was run again, for the retro's test-run count (scripts/retro_numbers.py test_run_counts). Closed variety (FR-13, AR-1): the cause words (`words`, one per cause, the plain words a person reads), and the tables that map a recorded field to one of them. A cause is read from a STRUCTURED field the controller or the runner recorded (the launch purpose, the dispatch's repair_cause in state/events.jsonl, the status of the previous attempt of the same test, a triage verdict), never from the prose of a `reason` (FR-12). Order of the lookup, first hit wins: by_purpose, then first_run (a test not seen before), then by_repair_cause, then by_previous_status (the attempt before this one on the same test), then a stand signal on that previous run's summary (lifts launch_failed to environment), then by_triage_verdict; no hit is `unknown`, never a default (FR-41). A null value in by_purpose means the purpose is known and says nothing about the cause, so the lookup goes on. A purpose that is not a key of by_purpose and not in not_a_run_purposes is unknown. A null in by_triage_verdict marks a verdict that is not a cause of a re-run, so the lookup goes on and ends at unknown (NOT_EXECUTED: nothing ran; FLAKY, APP_CHANGED, CASE_DEFECT, ASSERT_STRICTER: a person or a role decides, no cause is assumed for them; RUNNER_MISREAD_EVIDENCE: the runner judges the same captures again, nothing is run, so no cause of a re-run; NO_DEFECT: an observation of a manual check judged not a bug, nothing is run again). launch_failed is deliberately one word for two owners: the record does not tell an environment fault from a factory fault, and the retro says so.

words.launch_failed: after a launch that failed (environment or factory, not told apart)
